main.claim: Open a PDF in your browser, and the page reads its text aloud with your browser's voices. Pick a voice and speed, then press play, pause or stop. Scanned PDFs with no text layer can't be read here.

sections.heading: How to read a PDF aloud
sections.body:
Read PDF Aloud opens a PDF on your device, pulls out its text and reads it to you with the voices your browser offers. You don't install anything. Open the page, choose your file and press play.

1. Open [Read PDF Aloud](https://read-pdf-aloud.lazur.app/).
2. Choose the PDF you want to hear.
3. Pick a voice from the list.
4. Set the speed you want.
5. Press play.

While it reads, the page shows the part it is reading now, so you can follow along on screen as you listen.

sections.heading: Play, pause and stop
sections.body:
**Play** starts the reading from the text on the page. **Pause** holds it where it is, and pressing play again carries on. **Stop** ends the reading.

It is simplest to set the voice and speed before you press play. Listen to the first paragraph, then adjust if you need to. A speed that sounds right for a short note can feel too fast for a long report, so give yourself a minute to settle on one.

sections.heading: Why some PDFs won't read
sections.body:
A PDF can hold text in two ways. Most PDFs made from a word processor, a web page or an email have a text layer: the words are stored as text, and the tool can read them. A scanned PDF is a picture of each page, so there are no words for the tool to read. The page tells you when a file has no text.

To check your file yourself, try to select a word in your PDF viewer. If you can highlight the word, the text layer is there and the tool can read the file. If you can't, the file is a scan. For a scanned file, the page suggests [PDF to Text](https://pdf-to-text.lazur.app/) as the next step.

sections.heading: Voices and speed
sections.body:
The voices are the ones your browser provides, so the list depends on your device and browser. Some voices are easier to follow than others. Try two or three on the first page of a long file before you settle on one.

Start at a normal speed. Move it up only if you can follow the words without strain. A slower speed suits a document you want to take in closely, and a faster one works when you only want the main points of a long file.

sections.heading: When to use it
sections.body:
Read PDF Aloud fits reports you need to hear, contracts you want to check by ear, long articles saved as PDF, and study notes you want to review while you walk. Listening also catches the awkward sentence that looked fine on the page.

If you dictate on a Mac, Lazur types what you say in any app: hold two keys and speak. Windows is coming.

pages.title: Read PDF Aloud on iPhone: Steps and Settings | Lazur
pages.description: Read a PDF aloud on your iPhone in your browser. Choose the file, pick a voice and speed, then tap play. Also covers Speak Selection for text on screen.
pages.claim: Open Read PDF Aloud in Safari or another browser on your iPhone, choose a PDF, pick a voice and speed, and tap play. The page shows the part it is reading. Scanned PDFs with no text layer can't be read.

sections.heading: How to read a PDF on iPhone
sections.body:
Open Read PDF Aloud in Safari or another browser on your iPhone. The steps are the same as on a computer, with taps in place of clicks.

1. Open [Read PDF Aloud](https://read-pdf-aloud.lazur.app/).
2. Tap to choose your PDF. Pick it from the Files app or from wherever you saved it.
3. Tap a voice from the list.
4. Set the speed, then tap play.

The page shows the part it is reading, so you can follow the text on your screen while you listen. Pause holds the reading and play carries on. Stop ends it.

sections.heading: Voices on iPhone
sections.body:
The voices come from your iPhone's browser, so the list is the set your phone offers. It can be short or long depending on the languages your phone has installed. Tap a voice and listen to a sentence or two before you start a long file.

The phone speaker is small, so a voice that sounds clear on headphones can be harder to follow out loud. If you can, try the same file both ways and keep the setup that is easier for you to follow. A long file takes a while to get through, so pick a speed you can keep up with from start to finish.

sections.heading: Read text on screen with Speak Selection
sections.body:
Your iPhone also has a built-in setting for text already on screen, such as a web page, an email or a note. Go to Settings, then Accessibility, then Spoken Content, and turn on Speak Selection. Highlight the text you want, then tap Speak in the menu that appears.

Speak Selection reads the text you pick, one selection at a time. For a whole PDF file, use Read PDF Aloud above, because it gives you play, pause and stop controls for the file.

sections.heading: When the PDF won't read
sections.body:
Some PDFs have no text the tool can read. These are usually scans, where each page is a picture. The page tells you when this happens.

To check the file yourself, try to highlight a word in the PDF on your iPhone. If the word highlights, the text is there. If it doesn't, the file is a scan. The page suggests [PDF to Text](https://pdf-to-text.lazur.app/) for these files. If the file is a scan, a copy made from the original Word or Google Docs file often has the text layer you need.

sections.heading: What happens to your file
sections.body: The tool opens the PDF on your device and pulls out its text there. You choose the file yourself, and reading starts from the text it found. When you are done, close the page. The PDF stays where it was saved, in your Files app or your downloads.

faq.q: How do I get my PDF to read out loud?
faq.a: Open Read PDF Aloud in your iPhone browser, tap to choose the PDF, pick a voice and speed, and tap play. The page reads the text in the file out loud and shows the part being read. If the file is a scan with no text layer, it can't be read here, and the page suggests PDF to Text.

faq.q: Is there a read aloud option on iPhone?
faq.a: Yes. Go to Settings, then Accessibility, then Spoken Content, and turn on Speak Selection. It reads text you highlight on screen, one selection at a time. For a whole PDF, Read PDF Aloud gives you play, pause and stop controls for the file.

faq.q: Can I get my phone to read a PDF to me?
faq.a: Yes, with Read PDF Aloud. Open the page in your iPhone browser, choose the PDF and tap play. The voices come from your browser. If the PDF is a scan with no text layer, the tool can't read it, and the page suggests PDF to Text for that kind of file.

pages.claim: Open Read PDF Aloud in your Android browser, choose a PDF, pick a voice and speed, and tap play. For text already on screen, highlight it and choose Read aloud from the pop-up menu. Scanned PDFs need a text layer.

sections.heading: How to read a PDF on Android
sections.body:
Open Read PDF Aloud in your Android browser, such as Chrome. The steps are the same as on a computer, with taps in place of clicks.

1. Open [Read PDF Aloud](https://read-pdf-aloud.lazur.app/).
2. Tap to choose your PDF from your phone's storage or downloads.
3. Tap a voice from the list.
4. Set the speed, then tap play.

Use pause to hold the reading and play to carry on. Stop ends it. The page shows the part it is reading, so you can follow along.

sections.heading: Voices on Android
sections.body:
The voices come from your browser, so they can differ from one Android phone to the next. Tap a voice and listen to one or two sentences before you start a long file.

If a voice is hard to follow, change the speed before you change the voice. A slower speed often helps more than a new voice, and you can switch back at any time. The list only shows what your browser offers, and this tool can't add voices of its own.

sections.heading: Read text on screen with Select to Speak
sections.body:
Android has a built-in option for text already on your screen, such as a web page or an email. Highlight the text, open More in the pop-up menu, and choose Read aloud. This works without turning anything on.

For the shortcut version, go to Settings, then Accessibility, then Select to Speak, and turn on the Select to Speak shortcut. To keep reading while you scroll or switch apps, open Select to Speak, tap Settings, and turn on Read in background. Select to Speak might not work with every mobile browser. The full steps are in [Google's Select to Speak help](https://support.google.com/accessibility/android/answer/7349565).

sections.heading: When the PDF won't read
sections.body:
Some PDFs have no text the tool can read. These are usually scans, where each page is a picture. The page tells you when this happens.

To check the file, try to highlight a word in the PDF on your phone. If the word highlights, the text is there. If it doesn't, the file is a scan. The page suggests [PDF to Text](https://pdf-to-text.lazur.app/) for these files. If the file is a scan, a copy made from the original Word or Google Docs file often has the text layer you need.

sections.heading: What happens to your file
sections.body: The tool opens the PDF on your device and pulls out its text there. You choose the file yourself, and reading starts from the text it found. When you are done, close the page. The PDF stays in the place where your phone saved it.

faq.q: How do I make a PDF read aloud on Android?
faq.a: Open Read PDF Aloud in your Android browser, tap to choose the PDF, pick a voice and speed, and tap play. The tool reads the text in the PDF with your browser's voices and shows the part being read. A scanned PDF with no text layer can't be read, and the page suggests PDF to Text for those files.

faq.q: Is there a way for a PDF to be read aloud?
faq.a: Yes. Read PDF Aloud opens the PDF, pulls out its text and reads it with play, pause and stop controls, plus a choice of voice and speed. For text already on screen, Android's Read aloud option in the pop-up menu reads a highlighted selection.

faq.q: How do I turn on read aloud on Android?
faq.a: For a PDF, open Read PDF Aloud, choose the file and tap play. You don't need to change a setting for this. For text on screen, highlight it, open More in the pop-up menu and choose Read aloud. To use the Select to Speak shortcut, go to Settings, then Accessibility, then Select to Speak.

sections.heading: How to read a PDF out loud
sections.body:
Read PDF Aloud runs in your browser, so there is nothing to install. The steps are short.

1. Open [Read PDF Aloud](https://read-pdf-aloud.lazur.app/).
2. Choose the PDF you want to hear.
3. Pick a voice from the list.
4. Set the speed.
5. Press play.

The page shows the part it is reading, so you can follow the text as you listen. If you want the steps for a phone, the [iPhone steps](https://read-pdf-aloud.lazur.app/iphone) and [Android steps](https://read-pdf-aloud.lazur.app/android) are on their own pages.

sections.heading: Play, pause and stop
sections.body:
**Play** starts the reading, or carries on from where you paused. **Pause** holds the reading, and pressing play again continues it. **Stop** ends the reading.

While the PDF is being read, the page marks the current part, so a pause is easy to pick up again. Use pause when you need to step away from the screen for a moment, and stop when you are finished with the file.

sections.heading: What it can and can't read
sections.body:
The reader needs the text inside the PDF. Most PDFs made from a word processor, a web page or an email have that text. A scanned PDF is a picture of each page, so there is no text to read, and the page says so.

To check, try to highlight a word in your PDF viewer. If you can, the text is there. If you can't, the file is a scan, and the page suggests [PDF to Text](https://pdf-to-text.lazur.app/) for it.

sections.heading: Pick the voice and speed
sections.body:
The voices are the ones your browser provides, so the list depends on your device and browser. Listen to one or two sentences from each voice you are unsure about, and keep the one you can follow without effort.

Start at a normal speed. If you can follow every word, you can go faster. If you miss words or lose your place, slow down. A slower speed is the easier fix for most files. Test each voice on a full paragraph, not one line, so you hear how it handles longer sentences.

sections.heading: Good uses for a PDF read aloud
sections.body:
People use a PDF read aloud for long reports, study notes, contracts they want to check carefully, and articles saved as PDF. Hearing the text is a good way to catch a sentence that reads oddly, a number that is out of place, or a step that is missing.

Use the pause control when you need a break, and come back to the same file later. Keep the speed where you can follow it, not where it sounds fastest. Listening in short sessions works well for a long file. Pause, then play again when you are ready.

faq.q: What app can I use to read PDFs out loud?
faq.a: You can use Read PDF Aloud in your browser, with nothing to download. Open the page, choose a PDF, pick a voice and speed, and press play. Phone steps for iPhone and Android are on their own pages, linked above.

Not in this tool. The reader needs the text inside the PDF. A scanned PDF is a picture of each page, so there is no text to read, and the page says so. For a scanned file, the page suggests PDF to Text.

faq.q: Does the PDF leave my device?
faq.a: The tool opens the PDF on your device and pulls out its text there. Reading starts from that text, and the page shows the part being read as it goes.
